newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, focus on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, focus on liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in dull early Tuesday trading, with the focus on a relatively tight money market, dealers said.
"It's a slow morning. Operators are looking more into the money market," one U.S. bank dealer said.
The dealer said spot rupiah was trading in a narrow-range between the 2,370 and 2,371 levels.
He said the expected weekly rupiah depreciation of three to four points and the 2.7 points weekly swap premiums gave little incentive for operators to sell dollars.
One local bank dealer said the market had also no reason to go long on dollars because of the underlying liquidity concern due to the approaching month-end and festivities.
The lunar New Year celebration is due on February 7, and Eid al-Fitr celebrations on February 9 and 10, a market holiday.
Spot rupiah was at 2,370.40/70.75 at 0300 GMT against an opening of 2,370.0/70.5. Its early low was 2,370.75.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were quoted at 2,369.80/70.20 and 2,369.0/69.6, respectively.
Short-term swaps were seen driven by volatile money market liquidity in the morning, while longer-term rates were stable.
Overnight swap fell to 0.45 from 0.6/0.8 points. Tom/next swap was at 0.45/0.48 points.
The local bank dealer said there was some commercial demand for value today dollars which helped induce some rupiah.

The U.S. bank dealer said swap premiums were likely to be trapped at their present levels on fears that the central bank fixing might soon catch up market rates which could induce additional liquidity and increased pressure on swaps.
"In fact, swap rates are pretty cheap now," he said.
One-month swaps were at 12.10/12.60, two at 22.60/23.60, three at 34.25/34.75 and six at 72.50/73.00 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,368.0/2.560 and the conversion band to 2,368/2,416 on Monday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by four points last week.
